decision.trend: The trend in the research is to explore the effects of varying processing routes and conditions on the microstructure and mechanical properties of high-entropy alloys (HEAs), with a focus on refractory HEAs. The studies have shown that different processing routes, such as selective laser melting (SLM), spark plasma sintering (SPS), and high-pressure torsion (HPT), can lead to distinct microstructures and properties. The research has also highlighted the importance of controlling the oxygen content and porosity in HEAs to achieve optimal properties.
decision.unsolved: The unsolved problem is to understand the individual effects of changing the percentage of elements on the mechanical properties of HfNbTaTiZr-HEA. While the research has explored the overall mechanical properties of HEAs, the specific effects of varying the composition of individual elements remain unknown.
decision.why: A controlled variable experiment is the most plausible next step to investigate the effects of changing the percentage of elements on the mechanical properties of HfNbTaTiZr-HEA. By systematically varying the composition of individual elements, researchers can isolate the specific effects of each element on the mechanical properties, providing valuable insights into the underlying mechanisms and guiding the development of optimized HEA compositions.
